messages:
Avi R: Quick follow-up from last week's private-networking RFC. I sketched an incremental cutover for the 'egress-bridge' approach: sidecarless relay that preserves tenant src-ip via per-flow policy and a short-lived bind token. Goal: minimal change to customer VPCs, reversible at any step.
Sam T: Nice. High level: how does egress-bridge differ from the shadow-relay proposal?
Avi R: Difference is placement + authority. Shadow-relay inserted a tenant connector; egress-bridge runs in regional edge layer and uses a tenancy-tag propagated in packet metadata and an ephemeral bind token to avoid customer routing surgery. It's effectively a controlled hop, not a tenant-hosted connector.
Priya M: Concern: packet metadata requires ENI/iptables work in host VPC. Doable?
Avi R: Implementation plan: we use a connmark set by the ingress agent (already in customer VPC or via Privatelink) that the bridge reads. No kernel patching. Connmark lifecycle: set at initial SYN by the bridge-proxy, TTL 2m, refreshed per-connection.
Sam T: Where are we storing expected tenant-egress IPs? Need a single source for validation.
Avi R: cp-metadata cache (in-memory) with tenant->egress-ip ranges. Agents fetch on demand and reconcile every 10s. For canary we enable strict-mode: reject flows that appear to have switched src-ip outside allowed ranges.
Priya M: Can strict-mode cause false positives during routing churn? How to rollback?
Avi R: Canary plan: 1) staging integration tests 2) 1% tenant canary (48h) strict-mode off but metrics enabled 3) 10% with strict-mode on for 6h 4) 100% with gradual ramp. Rollback: flip strict-mode off and remove bridge routing entries.
Sam T: What are the rollout abort conditions?
Avi R: Abort if: a) >0.75% tenants in canary observe srcip deviations for >15m, b) p50 latency regresses >80ms for egress path, c) 5xx spikes >4% over baseline. We'll also monitor incomplete handshakes (bridge.bind.failures).
Priya M: How does the bind token work? Who mints it and how is it tied to tenancy?
Avi R: Token minted by control plane signer (cp-auth) per-tenant with 2m TTL. Token contains tenant_id and allowed-egress-subnets signed with CP's key. Bridge validates token via mTLS and signature. Also rotate signing keys hourly.
Sam T: For Private deployments customers may want local CA. Are we supporting that?
Avi R: Yes. Private installs can plug in their own CA; we support a CA fallback chain. Default: Redwood CP issues tokens for hosted/dedicated. Private: tokens can be minted locally by the operator with same protocol.
Priya M: Observability: what metrics/logs to add?
Avi R: Minimum: bridge.bind.success, bridge.bind.fail, bridge.srcip.mismatch.rate, bridge.path.latency.p50/p95, bridge.connmark.set.count. Logs: tenant_id, src_ip, observed_egress_ip, bind_token_id (redacted) - send to cp-trace-index with tenant label.
Sam T: Security: can a tenant spoof connmark to claim another tenant's egress?
Avi R: Not if we require bridge->ingress handshake and token validation. Connmark is set by the agent only after successful token exchange and mTLS. Also add attestation: ingress includes agent_fingerprint in token request so bridge verifies path origin.
Priya M: What about SNAT fallback? If bridge is down we must preserve connectivity.
Avi R: Fallback modes: passive (allow SNAT), conservative (drop flows not matching expected srcip), and redirect-back (route back to legacy connector). Default for hosted: passive fallback; for dedicated/private we make conservative optional. Canary will use passive to avoid customer outages.
Sam T: Any DB migrations or schema changes?
Avi R: No persistent schema changes. We add ephemeral entries in cp-cache and extend cp-auth to issue short-lived tokens. No long-lived DB writes.
Priya M: Ops runbook essentials?
Avi R: Short runbook: 1) query bridge.srcip.mismatch.rate for canary tenants 2) if >0.5% sustained over 15m -> set bridge in passive-fallback: POST /admin/bridge/fallback?mode=passive 3) to fully rollback: remove bridge routes and restore legacy connector entries 4) to validate, run tenant-sim curl tests against egress and compare to cp-metadata.
Sam T: Who owns the initial canary and pages?
Avi R: Owners: Priya M primary, Sam T backup. Escalation -> oncall-network. deploy-bot: Scheduled: egress-bridge-canary 2026-04-05T02:00:00Z (1% canary) Owner: Priya M.
Priya M: Timing looks good. I'll schedule staging load tests and sign-off once we have 12h of clean metrics.
Sam T: Please add a short note about tenancy migration: we keep legacy connector for 90 days after GA and offer migration helpers for big customers.
Avi R: Added: 90-day compatibility window + migration helper scripts (route export/import and token validator). I'll open a follow-up RFC with runbook, metrics queries, and the k6 scenario.
ops-bot: Noted. Added checklist item NET-5253: egress-bridge rollout docs to milestone 'networking-q2'.
Priya M: Cool. I'll review the follow-up RFC. Thanks all.
